title: Native ProofPath to LiminalDB handoff stops at the persistence frontier

ideaContract.purpose: Replace the synthetic ProofPath to LiminalDB heartbeat edge with native producer and consumer contracts while refusing to describe artifact compatibility as durable persistence.
ideaContract.expectedOutcome: A native ProofPath VALID receipt is projected into the dedicated canonical LiminalDB ProofPath AuditEvent profile, accepted by LiminalDB's exact artifact-only validator, and represented as an admissible LTP trajectory that explicitly stops before persistence.
invariants: the same logical_operation_id survives ProofPath receipt, LiminalDB AuditEvent and path trace
ProofPath producer provenance remains distinct from LiminalDB contract compatibility identity
the exact canonical ProofPath capability commit remains bound to the source evidence
the exact canonical LiminalDB ProofPath import contract and AuditEvent blob remain bound to consumption
artifact validation performs no durable write or live ingestion
evidence validation transfers no execution, mutation or persistence authority
the agent path reaches a stop-before-persistence state rather than silently crossing the unproven boundary
forbiddenOutcomes: relabeling ProofPath verification as a Lotus finding to reuse an unrelated validator
claiming durable memory from a dry-run compatibility PASS
treating historical repository commit as semantic contract identity
allowing persisted-evidence language to imply execution authority
skipping native ProofPath verification before LiminalDB projection
producing a correct final event through a path that omits the consumer validation stage
ideaContract.parentContract: NEO REZONANS heartbeat / ProofPath -> LiminalDB evidence transfer with authorityMode=NONE

evidence.claim: The upstream segment supplies a native ProofPath VALID receipt bound to exact SCIG bytes and canonical capability identity.
LiminalDB defines a dedicated ProofPath AuditEvent profile that is artifact-only and explicitly rejects durable/live persistence claims.
The generated SYSTEM-004 trace is inspected in strict mode with stable identity and continuity through the stop-before-persistence route.
The bridge separates ProofPath provenance, evidence digests, LiminalDB contract compatibility and consumer snapshot identity while carrying zero authority.
Negative controls reject logical-operation drift, receipt tamper, authority transfer, wrong consumer capability identity and false durable-memory claims.

past.summary: SYSTEM-002 represented ProofPath to LiminalDB as a synthetic heartbeat transition toward durable verified state; SYSTEM-003 made the upstream CGQA to ProofPath segment native.

present.summary: Canonical LiminalDB exposes a dedicated ProofPath artifact-only AuditEvent validator, not a durable ProofPath ingestion path. SYSTEM-004 makes that narrower boundary explicit and native.

future.summary: Durable ingestion is a separate falsifiable stage requiring namespace isolation, idempotency, transaction semantics, bi-temporal preservation, restart replay, rejection and rollback proof before the system map may call this edge persistent.

causalPath.statement: The whole-system shorthand labels ProofPath to LiminalDB as durable verified state even though the canonical consumer currently proves only artifact compatibility and explicitly performs no live ingestion.
The existing Lotus validator is semantically specific to LiminalQA Lotus findings and cannot honestly be reused for ProofPath SCIG verification.
A dedicated ProofPath AuditEvent profile binds native ProofPath evidence to the current LiminalDB AuditEvent contract while hard-coding artifact-only, zero-authority semantics.
The exact canonical LiminalDB validator consumes the generated event and produces a dry-run compatibility report with write_performed=false and durable_memory_accepted=false.
A native LTP strict trace audit verifies identity and continuity across ProofPath verification, projection, LiminalDB validation and explicit stop-before-persistence.

navigation.reason: The missing guarantee sits at a sibling repository transfer boundary and in the trajectory that reaches it, not inside ProofPath or LiminalDB core semantics alone.

refactor.change: Introduce a dedicated ProofPath-to-LiminalDB artifact bridge and validate it with the canonical LiminalDB consumer plus an LTP strict trajectory, while explicitly stopping before durable persistence.
refactor.expectedEffect: The next heartbeat segment becomes native without fabricating persistence, reusing an unrelated Lotus identity, or widening authority.

authorization.authorityBoundary: SYSTEM-004 proves a native evidence handoff only up to the LiminalDB persistence frontier. No durable write, runtime mutation, deployment, merge, financial action or external effect is authorized.
